Subject: Performance MAP: KV-cache impact & long-context close timeline

Hi Clara —

Following up from last week’s demo. Per our conversation I’ve attached a concise MAP and the evaluation plan we discussed so we can close on sizing and timeline. High level:

- Goal: validate 8k/16k/32k/64k context behavior and quantify TTFT, throughput (tokens/sec), and latency p50/p95 under increasing concurrency.
- Matrix: cold vs warm KV cache, prompt-length distributions (short/medium/long), batch sizes 1/4/8, concurrency 1/8/32/64.
- Success criteria (suggested): p95 latency <= 550ms at 16k seq for concurrency <= 8; TTFT (time-to-first-token) <= 220ms for typical 2–4k prompts; graceful degradation at 32k/64k with documented fallback to shorter variant.

Proposed evaluation schedule (suggested MAP milestones):
1) 10/25–10/26: test harness run — baseline cold-cache runs (low concurrency)
2) 10/27: warm-cache runs & concurrency ramp (Karthik to run)
3) 10/28: results review + SLA/commit draft (Marissa + Sean)
4) 10/29: finalize close (DocuSign link)

Attachments: hyperion_map_v1.xlsx (MAP with milestones), perf_harness_config.yaml (benchmark config).

Ask: Can you confirm that EngOps can provide an isolated test key and a sample prompt distribution (CSV) by EOD 10/25? With that we’ll run the harness during your low-traffic window.

Thanks —

On Mon, Oct 25, 2027 at 10:14 AM Clara Brooks <clara.brooks@hyperion.ai> wrote:
> For the 64k sequence tests, do you want us to spool synthetic repeated context or realistic long-document prompts? We can provide both but want to optimize runtime.

Clara / team —

We ran the full matrix today against the dedicated instance. Results (summary) are attached (hyperion_perf_results_20271027.csv) — below are the highlights. I’ll push a full dashboard link to the shared drive after this note.

Key takeaways:
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): cold KV cache averages 420ms at 16k seq (concurrency=1); warm KV cache reduces TTFT to ~180–210ms (16k, concurrency=1).
- Latency: p50/p95 at 16k, concurrency=8: p50 ~95ms, p95 ~480ms. At 32k p95 degrades to ~980ms (concurrency=8).
- Throughput: token throughput scales linearly up to concurrency=32 for short prompts; for long contexts (32k+) we see kernel memory pressure and throughput drops ~22% compared to 8k baseline.
- Concurrency behavior: stable scaling from 1→8; when pushing to 64 concurrency we observe increased tail latency and queueing; recommend burst-only mode above 32.
- KV cache impact: warm cache yields 2–2.5x improvement in TTFT for long-context requests (16k+); cold-cache penalties are most visible in throughput for chained multi-call prompts.

Notable failure modes observed:
- 64k synthetic repeated-context runs triggered intermittent OOM recovery on the smallest instance class — we recommend switching to a larger instance for full 64k SLAs.
- Prompt distributions with many short in-context examples (lots of short tokens but many KV lookups) increased p95 by ~15% versus single long-document prompts.

Action items proposed:
- Recommend production plan: enable warm KV caching + prefix caching for 16k use cases, reserve dedicated capacity for 32k/64k pilots with autoscale configured for warm-cache ramps.
- Marissa: draft the commitment language (SLA/Tier) and cost delta for reserving a larger instance class for 64k tests.
- Sean: schedule 30-min results review on 10/28 to go over numbers and finalize DocuSign.

Summary numbers (quick table):
- 8k seq, concurrency=8: p95 210ms, TTFT cold 140ms, warm 85ms, throughput 9.2k toks/sec
- 16k seq, concurrency=8: p95 480ms, TTFT cold 420ms, warm 195ms, throughput 7.1k toks/sec
- 32k seq, concurrency=8: p95 980ms, TTFT cold 920ms, warm 360ms, throughput 5.5k toks/sec
- 64k seq, concurrency=1 (larger instance recommended): p95 1.8s, TTFT cold ~1.6s (OOM risk on smaller instance)

Attachment: hyperion_perf_results_20271027.csv (raw run data), perf_harness_config.yaml (used config).

Karthik Iyer
Senior Perf Engineer, Redwood Inference
